answer.question: Are we on pace to hit goal, and where do we land by election day if nothing changes?
answer.answer:
No — at the current pace the program lands about 3,300 doors short of goal by election day, at roughly 94.6% of the 60,632-door target.

- Program to date: 33,503 doors, 103.3% of the 32,431 goal-to-date [table:v_office_pace]
- Projected total by election day: 57,329 doors, which is 94.6% of goal [table:v_office_pace]
- Shortfall if nothing changes: -3,303 doors [table:v_office_pace]
- 16 knocking days left at an average of 1,489.1 doors/day over the last 7 days [table:v_office_pace]
- To close the gap the program needs about 33.3 shifts/day vs. 29.3 now — roughly 4.1 extra shifts/day [table:v_office_pace]
- By office: Northside projects +908 over goal (104%), Harbor -1,007 (95%), Eastgate -3,204 (82%) [table:v_office_pace]

The projection is the last-7-day daily door average (1,489.1) multiplied by the 16 knocking days left, added to doors already knocked. [table:v_office_pace]

cases.question: Based on our pace and what's left, should we ask the client for more doors, or a second pass on the turf we have?

facts.name: doors we can knock in the days left

answer.question: Based on our pace and what's left, should we ask the client for more doors, or a second pass on the turf we have?
answer.answer:
Based on the program's own rule, we should ask the client for more doors first.

- Projected capacity for the rest of the program: 1489.1 doors/day × 16 days left = 23,826 doors [table:v_office_pace]
- Untouched (first-pass) doors still in our turf: 10,393 [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- Because capacity (23,826) is larger than the untouched doors left (10,393), we will run out of first-pass turf before the program ends [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]
- The rule says to ask the client for more doors first, since new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]
- A second pass on not-home doors (18,555 of them) is only the fallback, because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]

How it's worked out: projected capacity = average daily doors of the last 7 days × days left; if that exceeds the untouched doors left in the turf, we run out of first-pass turf and should ask for more doors before falling back to a second pass [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass].

args.query: should we ask the client for more doors or a second pass on the turf we have

args.sql:
SELECT
  (SELECT round(avg_daily_doors_last_7d,1) FROM v_office_pace WHERE office='All offices') AS avg_daily_doors_last_7d,
  (SELECT knocking_days_left FROM v_office_pace WHERE office='All offices') AS knocking_days_left,
  (SELECT round(avg_daily_doors_last_7d * knocking_days_left,0) FROM v_office_pace WHERE office='All offices') AS projected_capacity_remaining,
  (SELECT sum(doors_untouched) FROM v_precinct_coverage) AS untouched_doors_left,
  (SELECT sum(not_home_doors) FROM v_precinct_coverage) AS not_home_doors

In that case ask the client for more doors first; new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate. A second pass on not-home doors is the fallback, because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate. If untouched doors exceed capacity, keep working the turf we have.

cases.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?

answer.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?
answer.answer:
The client's sheet counts every attempt (each knock record) and is pulled before any QC rollback, while our dashboard counts each door once per day with rolled-back attempts removed — so the client's number is always equal to or higher than ours.

- Eastgate: client shows 498 "doors" vs 342 on the dashboard; the gap is 142 rolled-back attempts plus repeat attempts [table:v_daily_doors] [table:client_daily_report]
- Harbor: client shows 428 vs 406 doors; no rollbacks, so the 22-door gap is repeat attempts at the same door [table:v_daily_doors] [table:client_daily_report]
- Northside: client shows 558 vs 533 doors; no rollbacks, so the 25-door gap is repeat attempts [table:v_daily_doors] [table:client_daily_report]
- A normal day shows a gap of a few percent from repeat attempts; a larger gap (like Eastgate's) almost always means a rollback [doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours]

How it's worked out: the client's "doors" column is actually attempts pulled at end of day before QC rollback, while the dashboard counts each door once per day with rollbacks removed, so the difference is repeat attempts plus any rolled-back attempts [doc:client-reporting#daily-report] [doc:counting-doors#attempts].

args.query: client daily report doors counted attempts vs dashboard doors

args.sql: SELECT office, doors, contacts, attempts, rolled_back_attempts FROM v_daily_doors WHERE knock_date = '2026-10-12'
SELECT office, doors_reported, contacts_reported FROM client_daily_report WHERE report_date = '2026-10-12'

sources.sql: SELECT office, doors, contacts, attempts, rolled_back_attempts FROM v_daily_doors WHERE knock_date = '2026-10-12'
SELECT office, doors_reported, contacts_reported FROM client_daily_report WHERE report_date = '2026-10-12'

sources.text: The client daily report counts attempts, pulled at the end of each day before any QC rollback. Our dashboard counts doors with rollbacks removed. The gap on any day is the repeat attempts at the same door plus any attempts that were later rolled back. A normal day shows a gap of a few percent from repeat attempts. A larger gap almost always means a rollback.

An attempt is every knock record the canvassing app submits. If a canvasser knocks a not-home door at 11:00 and comes back at 14:00, that is two attempts and one door. Attempts are always equal to or higher than doors.

The client receives a daily report per office pulled from the canvassing app at the end of each day. It lists attempts (labeled "doors" in the client's sheet) and contacts as submitted, before any QC rollback. We do not edit a daily report after it is sent.

answer.question: Which precincts are untouched or only lightly touched, and is what's left dense enough to keep knocking efficiently?
answer.answer:
Seven precincts are untouched and four are only partially touched (no precinct is in the "light" band), and the remaining work is dense enough to keep knocking efficiently — the big untouched blocks are all well above the 2,000 doors/sq mi density threshold.

**Untouched precincts (0% touched):**
- P39 Harbor — 1,788 doors left, 4,094 doors/sq mi [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- P37 Harbor — 1,601 doors left, 4,039 doors/sq mi [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- P40 Harbor — 1,882 doors left, 3,676 doors/sq mi [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- P38 Harbor — 1,847 doors left, 3,304 doors/sq mi [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- P11 Northside — 890 doors left, 530 doors/sq mi [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- P36 Harbor — 766 doors left, 398 doors/sq mi [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- P24 Eastgate — 817 doors left, 281 doors/sq mi [table:v_precinct_coverage]

**Partially touched precincts (77–84% touched):**
- P23 Eastgate — 169 doors left, 504 doors/sq mi [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- P12 Northside — 185 doors left, 433 doors/sq mi [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- P35 Harbor — 134 doors left, 363 doors/sq mi [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- P20 Eastgate — 126 doors left, 1,503 doors/sq mi [table:v_precinct_coverage]

**Is it dense enough to knock efficiently?**
- The four big untouched Harbor precincts (P37–P40, ~7,118 doors combined) are all 3,300–4,100 doors/sq mi, far above the 2,000 doors/sq mi "dense" line, so they are worth knocking efficiently and even worth a new office [doc:program-plan#opening-another-office].
- The sparse precincts (P11, P36, P24, P23, P12, P35 — all under 1,000 doors/sq mi) are slow to knock and are better saved for drive-out shifts at the end [doc:program-plan#opening-another-office].
- The best candidate site for the dense Harbor block is the Mill Street storefront: 7,118 untouched doors within 3 km at $2,400/month [table:v_site_options].

How the density call is made: precincts under 25% touched that are over 2,000 doors/sq mi are "dense" and worth a new office, while those under 1,000 doors/sq mi are "sparse" and better handled with drive-out shifts [doc:program-plan#opening-another-office].

cases.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?

answer.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?
answer.answer:
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can physically walk to them and knock — specifically, 10 or more consecutive knocks recorded less than 30 seconds apart.

- Threshold: 10 or more consecutive knocks recorded less than 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Rolled-back knocks stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts, and rollbacks happen after the day's client report is pulled [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
- Every open flag needs a conversation between the field lead and the canvasser before the canvasser's next shift [doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]
- Two or more flash knocking flags in one week for the same canvasser go to the field director [doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]

sources.text: Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Rollbacks happen after the day's client report has been pulled, so they never change a report that was already sent.

Every open flag needs a conversation between the field lead and the canvasser before the canvasser's next shift, using the timestamped evidence on the flag. After the conversation the flag is marked reviewed. Two or more householding or flash knocking flags in one week for the same canvasser go to the field director.

cases.question: When does payroll run, and who has to approve overtime?

answer.question: When does payroll run, and who has to approve overtime?
answer.answer:
Payroll for the week that ended Sunday runs Tuesday at noon, and any shift that pushes a person over 40 paid hours needs the field director's approval.

- Payroll runs Tuesday at noon for the week that ended Sunday [doc:payroll-rules#payroll-deadline]
- Every shift must be approved by Monday at 5 PM; pending or needs_fix shifts left after that roll to the next payroll [doc:payroll-rules#payroll-deadline]
- Overtime threshold is 40 paid hours in a payroll week (Monday through Sunday), counting every shift worked [doc:payroll-rules#overtime]
- Hours over 40 are paid at 1.5 times the hourly rate [doc:payroll-rules#overtime]
- Any shift that takes a person over 40 hours needs the field director's approval and stays pending until approved [doc:payroll-rules#overtime]
- A shift marked needs_fix cannot be paid until a field lead corrects it [doc:payroll-rules#shifts-that-need-fixing]

sources.text: Payroll for the week that ended Sunday runs Tuesday at noon. Every shift must be approved by Monday at 5 PM; pending and needs_fix shifts left after that roll to the next payroll.

The overtime threshold is 40 paid hours in a payroll week, Monday through Sunday, counting every shift the person worked. Hours over 40 are paid at 1.5 times the hourly rate. Any shift that takes a person over 40 hours needs the field director's approval and stays pending until it is approved.

A shift marked needs_fix cannot be paid until a field lead corrects it. Common reasons are a missing clock out (no paid hours yet) and a shift clocked under the wrong office. Fix the record, then mark it approved.

cases.question: How should a canvasser record a locked apartment building?

answer.question: How should a canvasser record a locked apartment building?
answer.answer:
Record the building once as "inaccessible" on its first unit and move on — do not mark each unit individually.

- A locked building the canvasser can't get into is recorded once as "inaccessible" on its first unit [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units]
- Do not mark each unit in the building [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units]
- Marking a whole building from the lobby counts as householding [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units]
- Each apartment unit is normally its own door and must be knocked on its own [doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units]

sources.text: Pace compares doors to date with the goal to date. The projection for Election Day assumes nothing changes: doors to date plus the average daily doors of the last 7 days times the knocking days left. An office "will miss goal" when its projection is below its total goal; the shortfall is the goal minus the projection.

A contact is a knock with the result "canvassed", meaning the canvasser spoke with the voter. Not home, refused and inaccessible are not contacts. Contact rate is contacts divided by doors for the same period and office.
